summary: Revise at 6.2, up from 5.6. Round 2 closed the structural complaints from round 1. The cage is gone: the hip is now a smooth opaque orange-red oval 6.4 x 4.8, clear across its whole face, and the five-sepal calyx is a separate star at the hip's proximal end (side.png reads it well). stones.json is corrected. Prickles went from 10 to 29, the ring weighs 7.07 g instead of 4.7, and leaflets and sepal roots now pass the 0.8 mm wall. But the ring is not yet a Kings of Alchemy master piece, and three new or remaining problems hold it well below Caiman's 7. (1) The leaflets were thickened by inflation. They are now puffy pillows with crimped, stair-stepped edges and no sunk midvein (leaf-close.png, face.png). At 300 px the spray reads as laurel or olive, not rose, which weakens the plant read the ring depends on. (2) The hip sits in a plain straight-walled tube bezel, a mechanical collar that makes the hip look like a solitaire cabochon. The dome still shows concentric tessellation bands in face.png and stones.png. (3) The ground is still two bare twisted wires. There is no bark, 1 node per cane instead of the 4 asked for, side shoots that end in flat sawn tube ends (hero left, palm right, reverse lower right), and prickles in an even, comb-like row under the palm that reads as centipede legs. Gates: everything is green except the lost-wax wall gate, which the JSON does not fully record. 'Hip stalk' and 'Hip calyx, boss' are made parts with no ray_walls entry. Rose leaf 2 skips 2667 hard-edge faces and the Hip bezel 2483 (only 50 rays, min 0.815), against the round-1 acceptance limit of 1000. The gate string and lost_wax_note still say leaflets are judged at 0.15. An unrecorded gate is an automatic revise. One round remains. Reaching 7.5 needs every P0/P1 item below landed together. If the leaflets, bezel and cane ground do not all improve, round 3 should cut.
strengths: Round-1 P0 #2 is fixed. No metal crosses the hip. The dome shows unbroken over the whole stone, and the calyx is a separate five-pointed sepal star at one end (side.png, face-300). It no longer reads as a ship's wheel or a cage.
Round-1 P1 #3 is fixed. The hip is the specified opaque oval cabochon 6.4 x 4.8 (transmission 0.05, roughness 0.25, tint [0.72, 0.20, 0.06]), and stones.json agrees with report.json.
Leaflets and the sepal roots now clear the 0.8 mm lost-wax wall: leaflets 0.83-0.90, sepal bodies 0.85. The sepal points are reported separately at the detail floor, as round 1 asked.
Mass is up: 29 prickles (asked >= 28), 2 nodes, 2 side shoots, 7.07 g of 18k against 4.7. bare-vs-finished.png shows how much ornament was added to the twined canes.
The silhouette stays distinct: an open, twice-twined two-cane briar with an asymmetric crown spray, unlike any other Vepres ring.
The engineering stays clean: one shell, watertight, 0 degenerates and 0 crossings on all 51 made parts, 52 features Ok, 0 DFM, cold reload identical, a template of 288 KB with 1 patch.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Rose cane, prickles, leaves, hip and calyx only, thinning to cane and prickles at the palm. Nothing foreign appears.

checklist.item: Reads as its plant at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: Marginal, and weaker than round 1. In hero-300 and face-300 the inflated, crimp-edged leaflets read as a laurel or olive spray, and a solitaire cabochon in a tube bezel sits among them. Only the prickled canes and the sepal star (visible only in side view) say rose. A jeweller would more likely say 'laurel wreath with a carnelian' than 'wild rose with hip'.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: Leaflet margins are ragged and stair-stepped all round (leaf-close.png, stones.png left and lower right; face.png every leaflet). The teeth read as crimping on a pillow, not as forward-hooked serrations. There is no sunk midvein. The hip dome shows concentric tessellation rings and a radial pinch at its apex (face.png, stones.png).

checklist.item: Stones in made settings, visible, coloured as the plant's fruit
checklist.reason: It sits in a made bezel, fully visible, opaque orange-red, oval and the right size. The bezel's form is judged under the CAD item, and the tessellation under outlines.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms sculpted
checklist.reason: The hip bezel is a straight-walled cylinder collar with a flat top rim and a hard edge (stones.png, side.png). Both side shoots end in flat sawn discs (hero.png left, palm.png right, reverse.png lower right). The leaflets are uniformly inflated blobs, not modelled blades.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Not applicable: CAD-only, with no factory stock.

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Vepres rings
checklist.reason: An open twin-cane twine with an off-axis crown spray and a raised oval hip. No other Vepres ring is like it.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The large form (the hip) and the small forms (prickles) are there, but the medium layer is still thin. There is 1 node per cane (round 1 asked 4), no stipule collars, no bark. The prickles stand in an evenly spaced comb under the palm (hero.png bottom, side.png) instead of a rhythm graded toward the crown, and the shoulders at theta about 20-60 and 120-160 remain bare wire. Next to caiman/hero.png the ornamented share of the visible surface is still well under half of Caiman's.

punch_list.zone: ray_walls: Hip stalk, Hip calyx boss, Rose leaf 2, Hip bezel, Rose leaf 1 rachis, Hip receptacle; gate string and lost_wax_note
punch_list.change: Record a ray_walls entry for every made part, including 'Hip stalk' and 'Hip calyx, boss'. If a part owns no faces after union, sample it from its pre-union solid and say so. Resample Rose leaf 2, the Hip bezel and the rachis so each skips fewer than 1000 hard-edge faces, for example by splitting Rose leaf 2 into its leaflets and rachis as leaf 1 is, and give each at least 200 rays. Rewrite the gate line and lost_wax_note to name the true classes: bodies, leaflets and sepal roots at 0.8; prickle and sepal points at 0.15.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json ray_walls lists all 50 metal made parts (every made_parts entry except the cabochon). None skips more than 1000 hard-edge faces or has fewer than 200 rays. Every 0.8-floor part reads >= 0.8, and the notes name no leaflets at 0.15.

punch_list.zone: All 10 leaflets (Rose leaf 1 and 2), crown theta about 55-125
punch_list.change: Replace the inflated pillows with modelled blades. Keep a 0.8 mm thickness along a 1.0 mm-wide midrib band, and give the blade a flat-to-slightly-cupped upper face (0.2 mm sag), not a dome. Cut a sunk midvein 0.15 mm deep and 0.25 mm wide from base to tip. Give the margin a bevelled edge, sloping at 30-40 degrees from the face, so the silhouette stays thin while the wall stays 0.8 at the rib. Make 7-9 teeth per side, 0.2-0.25 mm, forward-hooked and fading toward the base, cut from a smooth outline sampled at <= 0.05 mm with no per-station stepping. Shape each leaflet as an ovate blade 3.2 x 2.0 with a sharper acuminate tip, terminal leaflet 1.2x larger.
punch_list.acceptance: In leaf-close.png every leaflet shows a crisp, continuous serrated margin with no stepped walls, a dark midvein line and a graded highlight across a nearly flat blade. In face-300, shown cold, the spray reads as rose leaves (pinnate, serrate, ovate), not laurel or olive.

punch_list.zone: Hip bezel and receptacle, crown theta 90; stone tessellation
punch_list.change: Replace the straight cylinder collar with an organic receptacle cup. The bezel wall rises from the receptacle with a 0.6 mm fillet, flares out 10-15 degrees, and is no more than 0.5 mm proud of the girdle. The top rim is rounded (0.3 mm radius), with no flat land. Model the receptacle as a hip's swollen base: a smooth urn that tapers into the stalk over 2 mm, so cup and stone together read as one fruit. Raise stone tessellation (at least 128 around and 48 up the dome) and fix the apex fan so the dome has no rings or pinch.
punch_list.acceptance: In stones.png and side.png no straight vertical wall or flat rim land is visible on the setting, and the gold flows from the cane into the hip. In face.png the dome shows one smooth highlight with no concentric bands and no apex star. At 300 px the hip reads as a fruit, not a solitaire.

punch_list.zone: Both canes, shoulders theta about 15-65 and 115-165, plus palm theta 200-340
punch_list.change: Add the missing medium layer and break up the comb. (a) Add 3 more leaf nodes per cane (4 per cane in all), each with a 1.6 mm swollen collar and a pair of stipule flanges 1.0 mm long, weighted to the shoulders. (b) Re-space the prickles irregularly (spacing varying 0.6-1.6x the mean). Alternate them up, down and outward, not all on the lower edge, scale shoulder prickles 1.3x the palm ones, and move at least 6 of the palm prickles to the shoulders. (c) Add bark: 0.08-0.1 mm longitudinal fissures, 3-4 per cane, on the side faces only. (d) Swell each cane from 1.4 mm at the palm to 1.8 mm at the crown.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero-300 and side.png every 45-degree sector of visible cane carries a node or at least 2 prickles. No run of 4 or more prickles has equal spacing and the same orientation, and the cane highlights break over bark. Side by side with caiman/hero.png at equal size, the shoulders are no longer bare wire.

punch_list.zone: Side shoots 1 and 2 (about theta 30 and 150 at the flanks)
punch_list.change: Finish each cut shoot as a pruned rose cane, not a sawn tube. Give the end an oblique 35-45 degree cut face with a 0.15 mm rounded lip and a domed pith, or turn the shoot into a tapering live tip ending in a bud 1.0 mm across. Add one prickle per shoot.
punch_list.acceptance: hero.png, palm.png and reverse.png show no flat circular disc on any shoot end.

punch_list.zone: Rose leaves 1 and 2 at the crown; calyx
punch_list.change: Make the hip read as a rose hip from the face. Turn the calyx star 15-25 degrees up so 2-3 sepal tips show past the bezel's distal rim in the face view, and add 2-3 pinnate side lobes to two sepals. Swap leaf 2's mirror for a rotated, slightly smaller (0.85x) copy with one leaflet pair folded 20 degrees, so the spray is not symmetric about the hip.
punch_list.acceptance: In face-300 the sepal tips show as a small gold star at one end of the hip, and the two leaves visibly differ in size and attitude.
